al.name: Alabama
al.fact: The giant Saturn V rocket that carried astronauts to the Moon was developed at NASA's Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville — nicknamed 'Rocket City'.

ak.name: Alaska
ak.fact: It's the largest state by far — more than twice the size of Texas — and Denali, at 20,310 ft (6,190 m), is the highest peak in North America.

az.name: Arizona
az.fact: The Grand Canyon, carved over millions of years by the Colorado River, is about a mile (1.6 km) deep in places.

ar.name: Arkansas
ar.fact: At Crater of Diamonds State Park, anyone can dig for real diamonds — and you get to keep whatever you find.

ca.name: California
ca.fact: It has the most people of any state, plus both the highest point (Mount Whitney) and the lowest point (Death Valley) in the lower 48 states.

co.name: Colorado
co.fact: It has the highest average elevation of any state, and its capital, Denver, is nicknamed the 'Mile High City' because it sits about one mile above sea level.

ct.name: Connecticut
ct.fact: The world's first nuclear-powered submarine, the USS Nautilus, was built in Groton and launched in 1954.

de.name: Delaware
de.fact: On December 7, 1787, it became the first state to approve the US Constitution — which is why it's nicknamed 'The First State'.

fl.name: Florida
fl.fact: The Everglades, a vast wetland nicknamed the 'River of Grass', is home to both American alligators and American crocodiles.

ga.name: Georgia
ga.fact: Civil rights leader Martin Luther King Jr. was born in Atlanta in 1929.

hi.name: Hawaii
hi.fact: It's the only state made entirely of islands. Measured from its base on the ocean floor, its volcano Mauna Kea is taller than Mount Everest.

id.name: Idaho
id.fact: It's best known for its potatoes — the state grows around one-third of all the potatoes in the US.

il.name: Illinois
il.fact: Chicago's Home Insurance Building, finished in 1885, is often called the world's first skyscraper.

in.name: Indiana
in.fact: The Indianapolis 500 car race has been held at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway since 1911.

ia.name: Iowa
ia.fact: It sits in the heart of the Corn Belt and is the nation's largest producer of corn.

ks.name: Kansas
ks.fact: The geographic center of the lower 48 states is in a field near the tiny town of Lebanon.

ky.name: Kentucky
ky.fact: Mammoth Cave is the longest known cave system in the world, with more than 420 miles (680 km) of surveyed passageways.

la.name: Louisiana
la.fact: New Orleans is known as the birthplace of jazz, and the state is divided into 'parishes' instead of counties.

me.name: Maine
me.fact: It's the only state whose name has just one syllable, and it's so famous for seafood that the American lobster is often called the 'Maine lobster'.

md.name: Maryland
md.fact: Francis Scott Key wrote the words to 'The Star-Spangled Banner' in 1814 after watching British ships bombard Fort McHenry in Baltimore.

ma.name: Massachusetts
ma.fact: Basketball was invented in Springfield in 1891 by James Naismith, and volleyball was invented in nearby Holyoke in 1895.

mi.name: Michigan
mi.fact: It touches four of the five Great Lakes and has the longest freshwater coastline of any US state.

mn.name: Minnesota
mn.fact: It's nicknamed the 'Land of 10,000 Lakes', but it actually has more than 14,000 lakes and other bodies of fresh water of 10 acres or more — and the Mississippi River begins here at Lake Itasca.

ms.name: Mississippi
ms.fact: The Mississippi River forms most of its western border, and its Delta region is often called the birthplace of the blues.

mo.name: Missouri
mo.fact: The Gateway Arch in St. Louis, 630 ft (192 m) tall, is the tallest arch in the world.

mt.name: Montana
mt.fact: In 1902, fossil hunter Barnum Brown dug up one of the first Tyrannosaurus rex skeletons ever found in its Hell Creek rock formation.

ne.name: Nebraska
ne.fact: It's the only state with a one-house (unicameral) legislature — every other state has two houses.

nv.name: Nevada
nv.fact: Most of the state is desert, and Hoover Dam, on its border with Arizona, holds back Lake Mead — the largest reservoir in the US.

nh.name: New Hampshire
nh.fact: In 1934, weather observers on Mount Washington recorded a wind gust of 231 mph (372 km/h) — a world record that stood until 1996.

nj.name: New Jersey
nj.fact: Thomas Edison invented the phonograph and worked on his famous light bulb at his laboratory in Menlo Park.

nm.name: New Mexico
nm.fact: Santa Fe, founded around 1610, is the oldest state capital city in the US, and Carlsbad Caverns has more than 119 caves.

ny.name: New York
ny.fact: The Statue of Liberty, a gift from the people of France, was dedicated in New York Harbor in 1886.

nc.name: North Carolina
nc.fact: The Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight near Kitty Hawk on December 17, 1903.

nd.name: North Dakota
nd.fact: A young Theodore Roosevelt ran cattle ranches in its Badlands in the 1880s, and Theodore Roosevelt National Park now protects that rugged land.

oh.name: Ohio
oh.fact: Seven US presidents were born here, and so were astronauts John Glenn and Neil Armstrong — the first person to walk on the Moon.

ok.name: Oklahoma
ok.fact: Its name comes from the Choctaw words 'okla' (people) and 'humma' (red), and dozens of Native American tribal nations are based here.

or.name: Oregon
or.fact: Crater Lake, which fills the collapsed crater of an ancient volcano, is the deepest lake in the US at 1,949 ft (594 m).

pa.name: Pennsylvania
pa.fact: Both the Declaration of Independence (1776) and the US Constitution (1787) were debated and signed at Independence Hall in Philadelphia.

ri.name: Rhode Island
ri.fact: It's the smallest state by area — only about 48 miles (77 km) long and 37 miles (60 km) wide.

sc.name: South Carolina
sc.fact: The first shots of the American Civil War were fired at Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor in April 1861.

sd.name: South Dakota
sd.fact: Mount Rushmore has 60-foot (18 m) carved faces of Presidents Washington, Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Lincoln.

tn.name: Tennessee
tn.fact: Great Smoky Mountains National Park, shared with North Carolina, is the most visited national park in the US, and Nashville is nicknamed 'Music City'.

tx.name: Texas
tx.fact: It's the second-largest state in both size and population, and from 1836 to 1845 it was its own country: the Republic of Texas.

ut.name: Utah
ut.fact: The Great Salt Lake is the largest saltwater lake in the Western Hemisphere.

vt.name: Vermont
vt.fact: It makes more maple syrup than any other state — about half of all the maple syrup produced in the US.

va.name: Virginia
va.fact: It's nicknamed the 'Mother of Presidents' because eight US presidents were born here, including George Washington and Thomas Jefferson.

wa.name: Washington
wa.fact: It's the only state named after a US president, and it grows more apples than any other state.

wv.name: West Virginia
wv.fact: It's the only state entirely within the Appalachian region, and it split off from Virginia during the Civil War, becoming a state in 1863.

wi.name: Wisconsin
wi.fact: Nicknamed 'America's Dairyland', it makes more cheese than any other state.

wy.name: Wyoming
wy.fact: Most of Yellowstone, the world's first national park, is here, and in 1869 Wyoming became the first US territory to give women the right to vote.
